messages.content: 你能估計2020年印度孟加拉虎的人口數量嗎？並將其與同年肯亞非洲象的估計人口數量進行比較，然後估計這兩種物種在各自國家的當前年份的人口數量嗎？

function.name: estimate_population
function.description: Estimate the population of a particular species in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which population needs to be estimated.

country.description: The country where the species lives.

year.description: The year for which population estimate is sought. Default is the current year.

And compare it with the estimated population of African elephants in Kenya in the same year, then estimate the populations of these two species in their respective countries in the current year." So we need to call the function estimate_population twice: once for species "Bengal tiger" or "tiger" in India for year 2020; second for species "African elephant" in Kenya for year 2020. Then we need to estimate for current year (which is 2026). So we need to call estimate_population again for each species and country for year 2026.

We should use the function calls. We can do multiple calls. We'll produce separate calls. Probably best to do four calls: 1) Bengal tiger India 2020; 2) African elephant Kenya 2020; 3) Bengal tiger India 2026; 4) African elephant Kenya 2026. Then we will output results. The function returns any type; likely numeric. We'll just pass arguments accordingly.

We need to ensure correct species names: "Bengal tiger" maybe recognized as "tiger". For elephants: "African elephant".

We'll call estimate_population with species: "Bengal tiger", country: "India", year: 2020. Then next call with species: "African elephant", country: "Kenya", year: 2020. Then same species but year default (current year). But we might specify year 2026 explicitly.
